article: ให้ลูกจ้างได้รับค่าจ้างไม่น้อยกว่าอัตราค่าจ้างขั้นต่ำรายวันตามที่คณะกรรมการค่าจ้างประกาศกำหนดคูณด้วยสามสิบ || EN: wage not less than the daily minimum wage set by the Wage Committee multiplied by thirty (cl. 13)
note: Fishers must be paid a monthly wage of at least the daily minimum wage set by the Wage Committee times 30, at least once a month (catch shares at least every three months), through the worker's bank account at the employer's cost. Editor question: The floor is the national daily minimum x 30; coded 2 because it is tied to the national rate. Editors may prefer 1 if a monthly conversion that ignores overtime is treated as a separate floor.

article: ให้นายจ้างจัดให้ลูกจ้างมีเวลาพักไม่น้อยกว่าสิบชั่วโมง ในระยะเวลาการทำงานยี่สิบสี่ชั่วโมง และไม่น้อยกว่าเจ็ดสิบเจ็ดชั่วโมง ในระยะเวลาการทำงานเจ็ดวัน || EN: employer shall give at least 10 hours' rest in 24 hours and 77 hours in 7 days (cl. 6)
note: At least 10 hours of rest in any 24 and 77 hours in any 7 days, with records for inspectors; in emergencies rest may be interrupted with compensatory rest. The LPA hours limits (s. 23, 8 a day, 48 a week) are not among the sections the Regulation keeps, so there is no limit on hours as such.

article: ถ้าออกจากงานก่อนครบสัญญาจ้าง จะทำงานกับนายจ้างอื่นใดมิได้ เว้นแต่จะพิสูจน์ให้นายทะเบียนเห็นว่าการที่ตนออกจากงานเป็นเพราะความผิดของนายจ้าง หรือได้ชำระค่าเสียหายให้นายจ้างเดิมแล้ว || EN: if he leaves before the contract ends he may not work for another employer unless he proves the employer's fault or has paid the former employer damages (RO 2017 s. 51)
note: A worker who leaves before the contract ends may not work for another employer unless he proves to the registrar that the employer was at fault, or pays the former employer damages (the recruitment costs, pro rata to time served); he must then start with the new employer within 30 days or the work permit and stay end. The restriction does not apply during a renewed contract. Cabinet rules on transfers for registered (non-MOU) fishers sit on ministry pages and were not checked. Editor question: Ss. 51-53 cover workers brought in under ss. 43/46 (MOU). Fishers registered under other routes (s. 63/s. 64 or cabinet resolutions) may follow different, ministry-level rules. Check? Official guidance supports unclear: This is general DOE guidance for documented workers whose papers are still valid. It is not specific to fishers, and MOU-route fishers follow the 5-ground rule (TH-MOU).

article: ผู้มีสิทธิจัดตั้งสหภาพแรงงาน…บรรลุนิติภาวะและมีสัญชาติไทย || EN: persons entitled to form a labour union must be of age and of Thai nationality (LRA s. 88); officers must be Thai by birth (s. 101(2))
note: Migrant workers may be members of a union (s. 95 sets no nationality condition), but only Thai nationals may found one (s. 88) and committee members must be Thai by birth (s. 101).

article: ในกรณีที่มีค่าบริการและค่าใช้จ่ายในการจัดหางานสำหรับแรงงานประมง ให้ผู้จัดหางานเรียกเก็บจากเจ้าของเรือ และเจ้าของเรือมีหน้าที่ต้องชำระ || EN: recruitment service fees and costs for fishers shall be charged to, and paid by, the vessel owner (WIF Act s. 11)
note: Recruitment service fees and costs for fishers are to be charged to the vessel owner, who must pay them. In general, licensed recruiters may not take money from the worker, and an employer who recruits directly may not collect recruitment-related money from the worker, except passport, health check, work permit and similar costs it advanced, deductible at no more than 10% of monthly pay. Editor question: Fees charged in origin countries are outside Thai law; s. 49 still lets employers recover passport, health and permit costs.

article: ลูกจ้างของกิจการเพาะปลูก ประมง ป่าไม้ และเลี้ยงสัตว์ ซึ่งมิได้ใช้ลูกจ้างตลอดปี || EN: [excluded:] employees of cultivation, fishing, forestry and livestock businesses that do not employ workers all year (Royal Decree 2017 s. 3(6))
note: The Social Security Act covers employees aged 15-60 without a nationality condition, and the Workmen's Compensation Act covers fishing employers. Fishing businesses that do not employ workers all year are excluded from social security. Vessel owners must also provide health and welfare benefits set by the Labour Minister (insurance or other means). Editor question: The SSA covers fishers on vessels operating all year; seasonal fishing is excluded. Keep 2, or code 1 for seasonal crews?

article: ให้นายจ้างจัดให้มีเอกสารที่แสดงหมายเลขโทรศัพท์ของกรมประมงและของหน่วยช่วยเหลือคนประจำเรือ ( Seafarer Help )…เพื่อให้ลูกจ้างสามารถที่จะร้องเรียน || EN: employer shall post the phone numbers of the Fisheries Department and Seafarer Help so workers can complain (cl. 19)
note: General complaint route to labour inspectors (LPA s. 123, kept for sea fishing by cl. 3). Vessels fishing outside Thai waters must give crew satellite messaging or calls (at least 10 MB or 15 minutes a month), and every vessel must post the numbers of the Department of Fisheries and Seafarer Help. Retaliation against complainants is barred, and disputes go to the Labour Court. A multilingual migrant hotline (if any) sits on ministry pages and was not checked.

article: คนต่างด้าวจะเข้ามามีถิ่นที่อยู่ในราชอาณาจักรมิได้ เว้นแต่จะได้รับอนุญาตจากคณะกรรมการ…ภายในจำนวนที่รัฐมนตรีประกาศตามมาตรา ๔๐ || EN: no alien may take up residence unless permitted by the Committee within the quota announced under s. 40 (Immigration Act s. 41)
note: Migrant fishers hold temporary stay tied to a work permit; the Immigration Act gives temporary stays of up to one year at a time, and permanent residence runs through an annual quota (at most 100 per nationality) with criteria set by the Immigration Committee. No provision was found counting time as a migrant worker toward residence. The 2+2-year cap on MOU employment is set outside the statutes reviewed. Editor question: The Immigration Committee's residence criteria and the MOU stay cap were not available on approved sites. Confirm 0?

article: คนต่างด้าวซึ่งจะเข้ามาในราชอาณาจักรเป็นการชั่วคราวได้จะต้องเข้ามาเพื่อการดังต่อไปนี้ || EN: aliens may enter temporarily only for the following purposes [list] (Immigration Act s. 34)
note: No provision was found in the Immigration Act or the Royal Ordinance on Foreign Workers that lets MOU or registered migrant workers bring a spouse or children. Temporary-stay purposes are listed in s. 34, with others possible by ministerial regulation (s. 34(15)) or cabinet exception (s. 17). Practice on dependants' visas was not checked. Editor question: The codebook's 0 means 'barred'. The law found is silent, not an express bar. Code 0, or 1 if dependants can obtain stay under s. 34(15) or cabinet rules?

article: Employment Act s 2: "employee" means a person who works under a contract of service, "but does not include any seaman, domestic worker or any person employed in a managerial, executive or confidential position".
note: Merged from BN-GEN (construction and agriculture); BN-DW shown where domestic workers differ. Construction and agricultural workers are "employees" and, if manual, "workmen" under the Employment Act. Only seamen, domestic workers and managerial, executive or confidential staff are excluded. Domestic workers (BN-DW) differ: value 1.

article: Minimum Wage Order para 2(1): "This Order applies to any employee ... under a contract of service for any employment specified in Schedule 1."
note: Merged from BN-GEN (construction and agriculture); BN-DW shown where domestic workers differ. The Minimum Wage Order covers only employees in the sectors listed in Schedule 1: banking, finance, ICT, telecoms and, since 1 April 2025, land survey, securities, private medical and education, security guards, tourism, travel agencies, architecture/engineering/QS firms and insurance. Construction contractors and agriculture are not listed. Editor question: Workers on Special Authorisation Work Passes (projects under one year) are excluded even in covered sectors (para 2(2)(c)). Architecture/engineering firms are covered; general construction contractors are not.

article: Employment Act s 65(1)(b): no employee shall be required to work "more than 8 hours in one day or for more than 44 hours in one week"; s 65(5): overtime not "more than 72 hours a month".
note: Merged from BN-GEN (construction and agriculture); BN-DW shown where domestic workers differ. At most 8 hours a day and 44 a week, 6 hours without a break, overtime at 1.5 times capped at 72 hours a month, and 12 hours a day in total; weekly rest day. The Commissioner may exempt employees from these limits (s 69). Domestic workers (BN-DW) differ: value 0.

article: Employment Act s 24(1): transfer "shall be subject to the consent of the employee and the endorsement of the transfer on the contract of service by the Commissioner."
note: Merged from BN-GEN (construction and agriculture); BN-DW shown where domestic workers differ. Transfer to another employer needs the worker's consent and the Commissioner's endorsement (s 24). The licence to employ immigrant workers is held by the employer (s 112), and the pass may name the employer, with the holder to stay in the specified job (reg 15). Company change-of-employer endorsements need a Labour Department transfer form. Domestic workers (BN-DW) differ: value 0. Editor question: Is the current employer's consent or release letter required in practice? If so, the value should be 0. The Labour Department transfer form could not be opened (labour.gov.bn, HTTP 401).

article: Trade Unions Act s 16(3): a non-citizen "may act as an officer of a trade union ... if he has been in continuous service with an employer in Brunei Darussalam for not less than 3 years".
note: Merged from BN-GEN (construction and agriculture); BN-DW shown where domestic workers differ. Same rules as for all workers: non-citizens may join, but may be officers only after 3 years of continuous service and residence in Brunei.

article: Employment Agencies Order s 31(a): an offence where a licensee "charges or receives ... for his services, any sum greater than the prescribed fee".
note: Merged from BN-GEN (construction and agriculture); BN-DW shown where domestic workers differ. Same agency rules as for domestic workers: agencies may charge only the fees provided by the Order or regulations; the regulations prescribe only licence fees. Editor question: Same question as BN-DW: is s 20 read as a full ban on fees charged to workers?

article: Workmen's Compensation Act s 27(1): "Every employer shall insure and keep himself insured with an insurer approved by the Minister ... in respect of any liability ... to any workman employed by him".
note: Merged from BN-GEN (construction and agriculture); BN-DW shown where domestic workers differ. Compulsory employer-bought medical insurance (at least $100,000; no wage deduction) and compulsory work-injury insurance with an approved insurer (Workmen's Compensation Act s 27; manual workers are covered whatever their pay). Editor question: The Workmen's Compensation Act text on AGC is the 1984 edition; check for later amendments.

article: Employment Act s 123: "This Part applies to all workmen and to other employees who are in receipt of a salary not exceeding $3,000 a month".
note: Merged from BN-GEN (construction and agriculture); BN-DW shown where domestic workers differ. The Commissioner of Labour inquires into disputes of workmen and of employees earning up to $3,000 a month (Part 16). Complaint forms are in Malay and English; no dedicated multilingual migrant channel was found. Editor question: Is there a Labour Department hotline with interpretation? labour.gov.bn was not reachable.

article: Immigration Regulations reg 15(2): an Employment Pass authorises stay "for such period not exceeding 5 years as shall be stated in the pass".
note: Merged from BN-GEN (construction and agriculture); BN-DW shown where domestic workers differ. Employment Passes last at most 5 years at a time, renewable. Permanent-residence categories (updated 31 December 2024) are based on family ties or descent, not on employment. Editor question: The long-term professional visit pass is for experts and professionals only. Confirm that no route exists for construction or agricultural workers.

article: Immigration Regulations reg 16(1): a Dependant's Pass may be issued to "the wife or dependant child of the holder of a valid Employment Pass, to enable the wife or child to accompany or join the holder".
note: Merged from BN-GEN (construction and agriculture); BN-DW shown where domestic workers differ. The wife or dependent child of an Employment Pass holder may get a Dependant's Pass at the Controller's discretion and against security; holders may not work without written consent. A husband is not covered. Editor question: Does Immigration guidance set a salary or job-level threshold that keeps low-wage workers from sponsoring dependants? None was found on immigration.gov.bn.

article: အကျိုးဆောင်လုပ်ငန်းကိုလုပ်ကိုင်လိုသူသည် အကျိုးဆောင်လိုင်စင် ထုတ်ပေးရန် ဦးစီးဌာနသို့ သတ်မှတ်ချက်များနှင့်အညီ လျှောက်ထားရမည်။ || EN: A person wishing to run an agency business shall apply to the Department for an agency licence as prescribed (s. 13).
note: Overseas employment agencies need a licence from the Department of Labour, approved by the supervisory committee; the licence can be refused, suspended or revoked, and running an agency without a licence is punishable by up to 7 years' imprisonment. Agencies must take responsibility for contacting the employer abroad when a worker's rights are infringed, but the Law does not make them jointly liable with the employer.

article: အကျိုးဆောင်လိုင်စင်ရရှိသူ မည်သူမဆို ကြီးကြပ်ရေးအဖွဲ့က သတ်မှတ်သည့် ဝန်ဆောင်ခထက် ပိုမိုတောင်းခံရယူကြောင်း ပြစ်မှုထင်ရှား စီရင်ခြင်းခံရလျှင် ထိုသူကို ထောင်ဒဏ် (၃) နှစ်အထိ ချမှတ်ရမည် || EN: A licensee convicted of charging more than the service fee set by the supervisory body faces up to 3 years' imprisonment (s. 27).
note: Service fees that the Department and agencies may charge are set under the Law (by the Central Committee, s. 6(g); s. 27 refers to fees set by the supervisory body); an agency that charges more than the fee set has its licence suspended or revoked and faces up to 3 years' imprisonment and a fine. The Law does not prohibit charging workers. Editor question: unclear: the fee amounts are set by committee decisions that were not found on mol.gov.mm; the value assumes a binding cap exists.

article: စာချုပ်ရှိပါက ယင်းစာချုပ်ပါ သဘောတူထားသည့် တာဝန်များကို အလုပ်သမားအတွက် ဆောင်ရွက်ပေး ရမည်။ || EN: If there is a contract, [the licensee] shall carry out for the worker the obligations agreed in it (s. 25(c)).
note: The 1999 Law does not require a written contract; it obliges the agency to carry out the obligations of a contract 'if there is one'. Contract signing between employer and worker before departure is handled administratively: an MOL announcement is titled on employer–worker contract signing and attendance at the overseas employment orientation course (mol.gov.mm post 37806; content not retrieved because the site blocked further access). Editor question: unclear: practice of signing contracts before the Department of Labour (MOL announcements) may support level 2, but no binding rule with minimum terms was found in official sources.

The 1999 Law only lets the supervisory body arrange training courses relating to overseas employment; it does not make orientation compulsory. MOL announcement titles refer to an overseas employment orientation course required in connection with contract signing and the Overseas Worker Identification Card (OWIC) (posts 37806, 35420, 34871; contents not retrieved). Editor question: unclear: whether orientation is compulsory for all workers and free of charge could not be confirmed from official text.

article: ပြည်ပတွင် အလုပ်ခွင်ထိခိုက်မှုအတွက် ရထိုက်ခွင့်ရှိသည့် လျော်ကြေး၊ နစ်နာကြေး အပြည့်အဝရရှိစေရေးအတွက်ဆောင်ရွက်ပေးရန် သက်ဆိုင်ရာ အကျိုးဆောင်မှတစ်ဆင့် တောင်းဆိုခွင့်ရှိသည် || EN: The worker may claim, through the agency, full compensation due for work injury abroad (s. 24(a)).
note: The 1999 Law creates no welfare fund and no compulsory insurance for overseas workers; it gives the worker a right to claim, through the agency, compensation for work injury abroad. Editor question: unclear: any compulsory insurance introduced by order or notification after 1999 could not be checked (mlis.gov.mm unreachable).

The 1999 Law does not provide for labour attachés. The MOL website lists Labour Attaché addresses (page 422, title only; content not retrieved), indicating posting by administrative decision. Editor question: unclear: no official MOL text on the posting of labour attachés was retrieved; level 1 rests on the absence of a statutory duty.

article: ပြည်ပအလုပ်အကိုင်နှင့် စပ်လျဉ်း၍ ရပိုင်ခွင့်နှင့် အခွင့်အရေးများ နစ်နာဆုံးရှုံးမှုအတွက် တရားမကြောင်းအရ ဖြစ်စေ၊ ပြစ်မှုကြောင်းအရ ဖြစ်စေ တရား စွဲဆိုခွင့်ရှိသည်။ || EN: The worker may sue, in civil or criminal proceedings, for loss of rights relating to overseas employment (s. 24(b)).
note: The Department supervises agencies and the supervisory body can suspend or revoke licences; the worker may sue in civil or criminal courts for loss of rights relating to overseas employment. No specialized body awards compensation.

article: ပြည်ပ အလုပ်အကိုင် သွားရောက် လုပ်ကိုင်ခွင့် မရှိသော ပြည်ပနိုင်ငံများ၊ လုပ်ငန်းအဖွဲ့အစည်း အမျိုးအမည်များနှင့် လုပ်ငန်းအမျိုးအစားများကို သတ်မှတ် ကြေညာခြင်း || EN: Designating and announcing the countries, organizations and types of work where overseas employment is not permitted (s. 6(e)).
note: The Central Committee designates the countries, organizations and types of work for which overseas employment is not permitted, and the Department may stop a worker found unfit by the medical board from leaving; these powers are sex-neutral on their face. Editor question: unclear: post-2021 bans or suspensions (including any sex-specific measures) could not be checked in official texts: mlis.gov.mm timed out and mol.gov.mm blocked access mid-session. MOL post titles seen but not read: an announcement on exit permission for workers returning on leave (post 43245), one on systematic checking of exit documents (post 42922), and one on family remittances of migrant workers through the Central Bank of Myanmar (post 44851, possibly related to the 2024 rule on remitting 25% of earnings). These need reading before coding.

article: ပြည်ပ အလုပ်အကိုင် အမျိုးအစားအလိုက် ရရှိခဲ့သော အတွေ့အကြုံနှင့် အသိပညာများ အတတ်ပညာများကို ပြည်တွင်းတွင် စနစ်တကျ ပြန်လည်အသုံးချနိုင်ရေးအတွက် လမ်းညွှန်ခြင်း၊ ကြီးကြပ်ခြင်း || EN: Guiding and supervising the systematic re-use at home of experience, knowledge and skills gained abroad (s. 6(d)).
note: The 1999 Law makes the systematic re-use at home of experience and skills gained abroad an objective and a duty of the Central Committee to guide and supervise, but it assigns no body a duty to provide reintegration services. Editor question: unclear: post-2021 remittance rules (MOL post 44851 on family remittances through the Central Bank, title only) and any reintegration program could not be read.

article: ទីភ្នាក់ងារជ្រើសរើសពលករខ្មែរទៅធ្វើការនៅបរទេស ត្រូវទទួលបានការអនុញ្ញាតតាមប្រកាសរបស់ក្រសួងការងារនិងបណ្តុះបណ្តាលវិជ្ជាជីវៈ || EN: Agencies recruiting Khmer workers for work abroad must obtain a licence under a Prakas of the MLVT (Sub-Decree 190, Art. 6).
official_link: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/ឯកសារផ្លូវការ/អនុក្រឹត្យ-សេចក្ដីសម្រេច/42-អនុក្រឹត្យ-សេចក្ដីសម្រេច/178.html
note: Private recruitment agencies need an MLVT licence and a USD 100,000 deposit held in an MLVT account, are inspected and can be warned, suspended or have the licence withdrawn. Prakas 252/2013 makes the agency pay unpaid wages first when the embassy confirms them before repatriation, but no general joint liability with the foreign employer is written. Editor question: unclear: Prakas 252/2013 Art. 8 obliges the agency to pay confirmed unpaid wages in full first; editors should decide whether this partial liability for wages reaches level 2 (joint liability).

article: ចំពោះចំណាយផ្សេងៗទាក់ទងទៅដល់ការរកការងារធ្វើនៅបរទេស ក្រសួងការងារ និងបណ្តុះបណ្តាលវិជ្ជាជីវៈនឹងពិនិត្យ និងធ្វើការណែនាំដោយឡែក ទៅតាមប្រទេសនីមួយៗ || EN: For costs of finding work abroad, the MLVT will review and give separate guidance for each country (Prakas 046/2013, Art. 7).
official_link: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/ឯកសារផ្លូវការ/កម្រងលិខិតបទដ្ឋានគតិយុត្ត/3732.html
note: Sub-Decree 190 sets no fee rule. Prakas 046/2013 leaves costs of finding work abroad to separate MLVT guidance for each destination; a 2026 MLVT notice fixes the service fee for farm work in Israel at about USD 3,800 and warns against overcharging. No general prohibition on charging workers was found. Editor question: unclear: fees are set by ministerial guidance per destination (e.g. Israel, about USD 3,800); guidance for other destinations was not found. Level 1 assumes these notices act as caps; if they are not binding, the value would be 0.

article: គំរូកិច្ចសន្យាដែលមានចែងក្នុងមាត្រា១៥នៃអនុក្រឹត្យនេះ ត្រូវកំណត់ដោយប្រកាសរបស់រដ្ឋមន្ត្រី... កិច្ចសន្យានេះត្រូវមានហត្ថលេខារបស់អ្នកតំណាងក្រសួងការងារនិងបណ្តុះបណ្តាលវិជ្ជាជីវៈ || EN: Contract models in Art. 15 are set by ministerial Prakas; the contract must bear an MLVT representative's signature (Art. 18).
official_link: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/ឯកសារផ្លូវការ/អនុក្រឹត្យ-សេចក្ដីសម្រេច/42-អនុក្រឹត្យ-សេចក្ដីសម្រេច/178.html
note: The agency must sign and carry out a contract with the Ministry, a recruitment service contract with the worker and an employment contract between the foreign employer and the worker. The employment contract must state working conditions, wages and benefits, be in Khmer, the destination language and English, and be sent to the Cambodian mission; contract models are set by Prakas and the contract must bear the signature of an MLVT representative. Prakas 253/2013 sets the minimum standard service

article: មុននឹងបញ្ជូនពលករទៅធ្វើការនៅបរទេស ទីភ្នាក់ងារជ្រើសរើសឯកជន ត្រូវធ្វើការណែនាំតម្រង់ទិសមុនពេលចេញដំណើរដល់ពលករឲ្យបានស្របតាមកម្មវិធី...ដែលក្រសួង...បានកំណត់ || EN: Before sending workers abroad, the agency must give pre-departure orientation following the Ministry's programme (Prakas 046/2013, Art. 9).
official_link: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/ឯកសារផ្លូវការ/កម្រងលិខិតបទដ្ឋានគតិយុត្ត/3732.html
note: Pre-departure orientation is compulsory and must follow the MLVT curriculum; it is delivered by the licensed agency in its training centre, and the Ministry issues a certificate that is required before the worker is sent. The texts do not say that orientation is free of charge to the worker. Editor question: unclear: the instruments are silent on who pays for orientation delivered by agencies; level 2 would need an official text saying it is free to the worker.

article: ប្រាក់ធានាដែលបានតម្កល់...អាចត្រូវបានដកយកមកប្រើប្រាស់...ចំពោះករណីប្រធានសក្តិ សង្គ្រាម កលិយុគ ជំងឺរាតត្បាត...ឬបញ្ជូនពលករមកកាន់មាតុភូមិវិញ || EN: The deposit may be drawn for force majeure, war, unrest or epidemics, or to repatriate workers (Sub-Decree 190, Art. 10).
official_link: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/ឯកសារផ្លូវការ/អនុក្រឹត្យ-សេចក្ដីសម្រេច/42-អនុក្រឹត្យ-សេចក្ដីសម្រេច/178.html
note: There is no statutory welfare fund or compulsory insurance for migrant workers. The agency deposit (USD 100,000) held by the MLVT may be used to repatriate workers in force majeure, war, unrest or epidemics, or when an agency fails to settle disputes; agencies must help workers obtain the destination's social security and bear the repatriation of the body of a worker who dies abroad. Editor question: unclear: the deposit is a guarantee held by the Ministry, not a fund or insurance; editors should decide between 1 (some risks covered) and 0 (no statutory fund or insurance). The 2019–2023 policy notes that social security for migrant workers is not yet arranged.

article: រាជរដ្ឋាភិបាលកម្ពុជា បានចាត់ឱ្យមានទីប្រឹក្សាទទួលបន្ទុកពលករ/អនុព័ន្ធការងារប្រចាំនៅស្ថានឯកអគ្គរាជទូត/ស្ថានអគ្គកុងស៊ុល...នៅប្រទេសទទួល || EN: The Government has assigned labour counsellors/attachés to embassies and consulates in destination countries (Labour Migration Policy 2019–2023, p. 14).
official_link: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/គោលនយោបាយ-និងផែនការ/2075.html
note: Labour attachés or officers in charge of workers are posted at embassies and consulates in Thailand, Korea, Malaysia and Japan by government decision. Sub-Decree 190 does not require them, and the 2019–2023 Labour Migration Policy notes that they are not yet in all destination countries.

article: ផ្នែកទទួល និងដោះស្រាយបណ្តឹងតវ៉ាទាក់ទងនឹងពលករទេសន្តរប្រវេសន៍ ត្រូវបានបង្កើតឡើងនៅក្នុងនាយកដ្ឋានមុខរបរ និងហត្ថពលកម្មនៃក្រសួងការងារ និងបណ្តុះបណ្តាលវិជ្ជាជីវៈ || EN: A unit to receive and resolve complaints of migrant workers is established in the MLVT Department of Employment and Manpower (Prakas 249/2013, Art. 1).
official_link: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/ឯកសារផ្លូវការ/កម្រងលិខិតបទដ្ឋានគតិយុត្ត/3732.html
note: A complaints unit in the MLVT Department of Employment and Manpower and the provincial labour departments receives complaints from migrant workers, including money claims, and conciliates them; agreements are binding, and unresolved cases leave the parties to their legal rights. The agency deposit can be used when an agency fails to settle a dispute, and agencies face warnings, suspension or licence withdrawal; there is no body that awards compensation.

article: ការផ្សព្វផ្សាយ ការជ្រើសរើស និងការបញ្ជូនជនទេសន្តរប្រវេសន៍ការងារខ្មែរទៅធ្វើការនៅក្រៅប្រទេសក្នុងវិស័យនេសាទ និងការដ្ឋានរុករករ៉ែ ត្រូវបានហាមឃាត់ជាដាច់ខាត || EN: Advertising, recruiting and sending Khmer migrant workers abroad for fishing and mining sites is strictly prohibited (Notice 27/26).
official_link: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/ឯកសារផ្លូវការ/សេចក្ដីជូនដំណឹង-សេចក្ដីណែនាំ/51-សេចក្ដីជូនដំណឹង-សេចក្ដីណែនាំ/3806.html
note: Migrant workers of both sexes must be at least 18. In September 2026 the MLVT banned advertising, recruiting and sending Khmer migrant workers abroad for fishing and mining work, and it has warned against recruitment for Russia and Armenia; the rules are sex-neutral on their face. Agencies are authorized separately for each destination (some lists concern female domestic workers).

article: សហការជាមួយមជ្ឈមណ្ឌលពលករទេសន្តរប្រវេសន៍មាតុភូមិនិវត្តន៍កម្ពុជា (HRCC) រៀបចំកម្មវិធីបណ្តុះបណ្តាលជំនាញវិជ្ជាជីវៈ និងសហគ្រិនភាព...ដោយឥតគិតថ្លៃដល់អតីតពលករខ្មែរ || EN: With the HRCC, the Ministry runs free vocational and entrepreneurship training for former Khmer migrant workers (Notice 22/26).
official_link: https://mlvt.gov.kh/index.php/ឯកសារផ្លូវការ/សេចក្ដីជូនដំណឹង-សេចក្ដីណែនាំ/51-សេចក្ដីជូនដំណឹង-សេចក្ដីណែនាំ/3728.html
note: Sub-Decree 190 only requires agencies to bring returning workers to the Ministry for a certificate of work done abroad. Reintegration rests on the Labour Migration Policy and programs: in 2026 the MLVT, with the Cambodian centre for returned migrant workers (HRCC), offers free vocational and entrepreneurship training and job referral through the National Employment Agency to returned workers.

article: ບໍລິການຈັດຫາງານ ທັງພາຍໃນ ແລະ ຕ່າງປະເທດ ໂດຍບໍ່ໄດ້ຮັບອະນຸຍາດ || EN: [prohibited:] providing employment services, at home or abroad, without a licence (Employment Services Law Art. 49(4))
note: Recruiters must register as an enterprise and obtain an operating licence from the Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare (MoLSW), and providing employment services without a licence is prohibited. Licences can be suspended or revoked. The agency answers for the interests of the workers it sends 'under the contract' and must compensate damage it causes, but no provision makes it jointly liable with the foreign employer.

article: ເກັບຄ່າບໍລິການບໍ່ໃຫ້ເກີນ ສາມສ່ວນຮ້ອຍ ຂອງເງິນເດືອນທຸກເດືອນຕາມສັນຍາ ສຳລັບການບໍລິການຈັດຫາງານໄປຕ່າງປະເທດ || EN: collect a service fee not exceeding three percent of the salary each month under the contract, for overseas placement services (Agreement 850/2026 Art. 13(6))
note: The 2020 Decree leaves fees and service charges to a Presidential decree issued from time to time. The 2026 MoLSW Agreement caps the overseas placement fee at 3% of each month's salary under the contract. Collecting fees above set rates and taking deposits or collateral from workers are prohibited. Editor question: unclear: the Presidential decree on fees named in Decree 245 Art. 18 was not located, and the percentage was read from a scanned image ('ສາມສ່ວນຮ້ອຍ' = 3%). Please confirm both.

article: ມີສັນຍາຜູກພັນ ແລະ ສັນຍາແຮງງານ || EN: [the worker must] have a commitment contract and a labour contract (Decree 245/2020 Art. 9(8))
note: Each worker must hold a commitment contract with the sending agency and a labour contract with the employer. The labour contract and the labour-supply contract are part of the licence file that MoLSW reviews before it licenses each sending. The Decree defines the labour contract as covering working conditions, wages, welfare and other terms, but sets no detailed minimum terms. Editor question: unclear: verification happens through MoLSW review of the licence file, but no state-set minimum terms were found. Level 1 is defensible if verification of content is not considered established.

article: ຕ້ອງໄດ້ຮັບການຝຶກອົບຮົມ ຕາມຫຼັກສູດທີ່ກ່ຽວຂ້ອງ ກ່ອນທີ່ຈະໄປເຮັດວຽກຢູ່ຕ່າງປະເທດ || EN: [the worker] must receive training under the relevant curriculum before going to work abroad (Decree 245/2020 Art. 11(4))
note: Training before departure is compulsory for the worker, and the sending agency must provide it. The province certifies the list of workers only after this training. No provision found says the training is free, or that it must cover rights and complaint channels. Editor question: unclear: nothing found on who pays for the training. Level 2 would apply if official rules make it free.

article: ມອບເງິນ ເຂົ້າກອງທຶນຊ່ວຍເຫຼືອຜູ້ອອກແຮງງານລາວ ທີ່ເຮັດວຽກຢູ່ຕ່າງປະເທດ || EN: pay money into the fund to assist Lao workers working abroad (Decree 245/2020 Art. 11(7))
note: Workers and sending agencies must pay into a fund to assist Lao workers abroad, and workers must join social security under Lao law and the destination country's law. Agencies must lodge a guarantee deposit with MoLSW for helping workers in emergencies. No rules were found on the fund's benefits (death, disability, repatriation, legal aid). Editor question: unclear: the fund's legal basis (the Decree points to the Labour Law) and its benefits were not found in the official texts consulted. The ministry site molsw.gov.la could not be reached.

article: ສະເໜີແຕ່ງຕັ້ງ ຜູ້ຕາງໜ້າດ້ານແຮງງານ ໄປປະຈຳຢູ່ສຳນັກງານຜູ້ຕາງໜ້າການທູດ ... ໃນກໍລະນີ ທີ່ເຫັນວ່າ ມີຄວາມຈຳເປັນ || EN: propose appointing labour representatives to diplomatic missions ... where deemed necessary (Decree 245/2020 Art. 25(5))
note: MoLSW may propose appointing labour representatives to Lao diplomatic or consular missions 'where deemed necessary'. This is a discretionary power in a decree, not a statutory duty. Sending agencies must also keep their own representative abroad.

article: ຍື່ນຄຳຮ້ອງ ຫຼື ຄຳສະເໜີ ຕໍ່ອົງການທີ່ກ່ຽວຂ້ອງ || EN: [the worker has the right to] file a complaint or petition with the relevant bodies (Decree 245/2020 Art. 10(9))
note: Workers may file complaints or petitions. MoLSW and the provincial and district labour offices must receive and resolve them, and can suspend or revoke licences. Violators may be ordered to pay civil damages, but no specialised body was found that awards compensation against recruiters or foreign employers. Labour disputes follow the Labour Law's mediation, administrative, committee and court routes.

article: ເປັນຂົງເຂດ ແລະ ເປັນປະເທດ ທີ່ຍັງບໍ່ມີສັນຍາຮ່ວມມືສອງຝ່າຍດ້ານການຈ້າງແຮງງານ ແລະ ຍັງບໍ່ມີຄວາມສຳພັນທາງດ້ານການທູດ ກັບ ສປປ ລາວ || EN: areas and countries with no bilateral labour cooperation agreement and no diplomatic relations with Lao PDR (Decree 245/2020 Art. 20(3))
note: The minimum age is 18. Sending is barred for listed jobs (for example prostitution, massage services, dangerous chemicals, sea fishing on small boats, mine clearance) and for areas or countries at war, or with no bilateral labour agreement and no diplomatic relations with Laos. All of these rules are sex-neutral on their face, and agencies may not discriminate by sex.

article: ຊຸກຍູ້ ແລະ ສົ່ງເສີມ ໃຫ້ຜູ້ອອກແຮງງານລາວ ທີ່ສິ້ນສຸດສັນຍາການເຮັດວຽກຢູ່ຕ່າງປະເທດ ປະກອບອາຊີບ ພາຍໃນປະເທດ || EN: encourage and promote Lao workers whose contracts abroad have ended to take up occupations at home (Decree 245/2020 Art. 25(9))
note: MoLSW and the provincial and district offices must 'encourage and promote' returnees to work at home and to upgrade their skills. This duty is in a decree, not a statute. Sending agencies must bring workers home when their contracts end. The Anti-Trafficking Law's statutory reintegration duties cover trafficking victims only.

article: Organizar e coordenar o processo de seleção e recrutamento de trabalhadores para participarem nos programas de emprego no estrangeiro || EN: organise and coordinate the selection and recruitment of workers for overseas employment programmes (DL 80/2023 Art. 11(2)(i))
note: No law or decree-law licensing private recruitment agencies for overseas work was found in the Jornal da República. The Labour Law applies only in the national territory. Overseas placement runs through SEFOPE's National Directorate for Employment Abroad (DNEE), which organises selection and recruitment for the overseas employment programmes. Editor question: unclear: the coding rests on not finding any law. jornal.gov.tl did not resolve (DNS failure), the SEFOPE site is offline, and AsianLII refused automated access, so a ministerial diploma or scheme rules may have been missed.

No legal limit on fees charged to workers for overseas employment was found in the Jornal da República. Editor question: unclear: no provision found. The Korea EPS and Australia PALM scheme rules could not be checked in official sources.

article: A presente lei é aplicável no território nacional, aos trabalhadores e empregadores || EN: this law applies in the national territory to workers and employers (Labour Law Art. 2(1))
note: No legal requirement for an employment contract before departure was found. The Labour Law covers only work in the national territory. Contract terms for the Korea EPS and Australia PALM schemes are set by those programmes, which could not be checked in official Timor-Leste sources. Editor question: unclear: the coding rests on not finding any law.

article: Realizar sessões de esclarecimentos aos trabalhadores que participam nos programas de emprego ao estrangeiro, nomeadamente antes da sua partida || EN: hold information sessions for workers in overseas employment programmes, in particular before departure (DL 80/2023 Art. 11(2)(j))
note: SEFOPE's National Directorate for Employment Abroad must hold information sessions for workers in the overseas employment programmes, in particular before departure. This applies only to programme participants. The decree does not say the sessions are compulsory for the worker or free, or that they cover rights and complaint channels. Editor question: unclear: this is a duty of the service, not an explicit obligation on the worker. Level 0 is arguable.

article: Os cidadãos timorenses no estrangeiro podem beneficiar de apoio do Estado em caso de repatriamento quando: a) Comprovem não dispor de meios financeiros || EN: Timorese citizens abroad may receive State support for repatriation when they prove they lack the means (DL 77/2022 Art. 4(1))
note: No statutory fund or compulsory insurance for overseas workers was found. A 2022 decree-law gives all Timorese citizens abroad means-tested, budget-dependent help (repatriation, emergency housing and food), which they must normally repay. It is not specific to workers. Editor question: unclear: insurance required by the Korea EPS or Australia PALM schemes may exist but could not be checked in official Timor-Leste sources.

article: Coordenar ... com os adidos de trabalho junto das missões diplomáticas timorenses no estrangeiro || EN: coordinate ... with the labour attachés at Timorese diplomatic missions abroad (DL 80/2023 Art. 11(2)(d))
note: The SEFOPE decree-law tells the National Directorate for Employment Abroad to coordinate with the 'labour attachés at Timorese diplomatic missions abroad', which assumes they exist. No legal provision found requires them to be posted. Editor question: unclear: the posting decision behind these attachés was not found. Level 0 would apply if no attachés are in fact posted.

article: Promover os serviços de mediação, de conciliação e de arbitragem no âmbito das relações laborais || EN: promote mediation, conciliation and arbitration services in labour relations (DL 80/2023 Art. 3(f))
note: No specialised complaint or compensation body for overseas workers was found. SEFOPE promotes mediation, conciliation and arbitration for labour relations in Timor-Leste, and trafficking victims may claim damages through the courts. Editor question: unclear: the coding rests on not finding any law.

No legal restriction on emigration for work was found in the Jornal da República: no destination bans, no minimum age above adulthood, and no rules for women only. Eligibility conditions of the Korea EPS and Australia PALM programmes could not be checked in official Timor-Leste sources. Editor question: unclear: the coding rests on not finding any restriction. Programme rules (age limits, for example) may set restrictions; if so, level 1.

article: Promover o programa de reintegração dos trabalhadores timorenses, após concluir conclusão do seu contrato trabalho no estrangeiro || EN: promote the reintegration programme for Timorese workers after their work contract abroad ends (DL 80/2023 Art. 11(2)(c))
note: SEFOPE's National Directorate for Employment Abroad must 'promote the reintegration programme' for workers after their contracts abroad end. This is in an organic decree-law setting the service's tasks, not a statute giving workers a right to reintegration services. Editor question: unclear: a decree-law has force of law in Timor-Leste. Editors may treat this as a statutory duty (level 2).
